context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations within 50 milliseconds. It provides automated scoring, case management for analysts, and immutable 7-year audit logs for a mid-size payment processor.

## Key Elements
- **Merchant / Payment Gateway System**: External system submitting payment authorization requests via REST API.
- **Fraud Analyst**: Internal user reviewing suspicious transactions via case management UI.
- **Risk Manager / Data Scientist**: Internal user updating scoring models and rules with zero downtime.
- **Merchant Support**: Internal user accessing read-only audit logs for dispute resolution.
- **API Gateway**: AWS API Gateway enforcing TLS 1.3, mTLS, and AWS WAF rate-limiting.
- **Scoring Service**: AWS ECS on Fargate containers executing fraud detection logic.
- **Case Management App**: Containerized backend for analyst review workflows.
- **Audit Storage**: AWS S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode and AWS Glacier lifecycle policies.
- **Key Management**: AWS KMS / CloudHSM with automated key rotation.

## Relationships
- **Merchant System -> API Gateway**: Submits authorization requests via HTTPS using TLS 1.3, mTLS, and API keys.
- **API Gateway -> Scoring Service**: Forwards transaction payloads via internal VPC networking using gRPC.
- **Scoring Service -> Audit Storage**: Streams decision payloads, inputs, and model versions to S3 with Object Lock via AWS SDK.
- **Fraud Analyst -> Case Management App**: Reviews flagged transactions via HTTPS/OIDC with MFA.
- **Risk Manager -> Scoring Service**: Deploys updated models and rules with zero downtime via CI/CD pipelines.

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: AWS ECS on Fargate with auto-scaling to maintain sub-50ms P99 latency within budget.
- **API & Protocol**: REST and gRPC for high-throughput, low-latency inter-service communication.
- **Security & Compliance**: AWS WAF, AWS KMS, CloudHSM, and TLS 1.3 for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.
- **Storage & Audit**: Amazon S3 with Compliance Mode Object Lock and S3 Glacier for 7-year retention.
- **Authentication**: OIDC/OAuth2 with hardware-token MFA for internal users.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a three-engineer team while meeting strict sub-50ms latency and PCI-DSS compliance requirements. Serverless container scaling and S3 Glacier lifecycle policies ensure the system stays within the strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time, executing fraud scoring and analyst case management for a mid-size payment processor. It ensures high availability, strict PCI-DSS compliance, and auditable 7-year tamper-evident decision logging.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst, Risk Manager / Data Scientist, Merchant Support (Users)
- Merchant / Payment Gateway System (External System)
- Scoring Engine Container (CDE private subnet)
- Case Management Container (Isolated external subnet)
- AWS ECS on Fargate (Container Orchestration)
- Amazon S3 Glacier & AWS S3 Object Lock (Data Retention & Audit storage)
- AWS KMS & AWS QLDB (Security & Tamper-Evident Ledger)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway to Scoring Engine Container via gRPC/HTTPS with TLS 1.3
- Scoring Engine Container to AWS QLDB and S3 via AWS SDK (mTLS)
- Fraud Analyst to Case Management Container via HTTPS (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC JWT)
- Case Management Container to Scoring Engine via internal REST/mTLS APIs
- AWS CloudWatch to PagerDuty via Webhooks for real-time alerting

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Selected for lightweight container orchestration suited to a 3-engineer team within budget.
- AWS QLDB & S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, WORM-compliant 7-year audit retention (R-06).
- AWS KMS: Provides AES-256 encryption at rest for tokenized card data (R-05).
- AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT): Monitors P99 latency below 50 ms at 3,000 TPS.

## Rationale
This architecture fits the requirements by strictly isolating the Cardholder Data Environment to contain PCI-DSS scope while leveraging serverless Fargate to stay under the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Automated fail-open mechanics with strict PagerDuty alerts guarantee low latency and high availability without compromising security.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
[System screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time, providing case management and explainable audit trails for analysts. Designed for a mid-size payment processor under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager / Data Scientist
- Merchant / Payment Gateway System
- Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS on Fargate, gRPC, HTTPS, TLS 1.3)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS on Fargate, REST, mTLS)
- AWS S3 with Object Lock (WORM)
- AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway System -> Scoring Engine Container: Submits payment authorization requests [gRPC/HTTPS with TLS 1.3]
- Case Management Container -> Scoring Engine Container: Queries and manages case details [internal REST/mTLS APIs]
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS S3 (WORM): Stores cryptographically signed decisions and immutable audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS KMS: Verifies model signatures and manages data encryption keys [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Runs containers within a fixed budget while supporting autoscaling
- gRPC / TLS 1.3: Ensures low-latency, secure communication for real-time scoring (<50ms P99)
- AWS S3 with Object Lock: Guarantees 7-year tamper-evident storage for regulatory compliance
- AWS KMS: Handles cryptographic signing of decisions and field-level data encryption (R-05, R-06)
- GitHub Actions: Automates zero-downtime model packaging and deployment pipelines (R-03)

## Rationale
[This architecture balances sub-50ms P99 latency and high availability with strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability. Leveraging managed AWS services keeps operations sustainable for a three-engineer team within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time payment fraud screening and case management for card-not-present transactions. It ensures rapid, auditable fraud decisions while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst
- Case Management Container
- Scoring Engine Container
- AWS S3 Object Lock Bucket
- AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Container: Reviews flagged transactions via HTTPS (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC JWT)
- Case Management Container -> Scoring Engine Container: Queries and manages case details via internal REST APIs (mTLS via AWS App Mesh)
- Case Management Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Streams cryptographically signed audit logs via AWS IAM

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Hosts containers with auto-scaling based on analyst session metrics to stay within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget
- AWS App Mesh: Automates mTLS sidecars to meet zero-trust requirements without manual certificate rotations for a 3-person team
- AWS S3 Object Lock & Glacier: Provides 7-year tamper-evident audit storage with automated lifecycle transitions
- AWS KMS: Handles cryptographic signing of audit event payloads for non-repudiation

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability with the operational constraints of a 3-person engineering team. Automated infrastructure and risk-based security controls maximize analyst productivity while adhering to a fixed budget.
